_comments: The four seeded contract types (plan §7 / ERD §7). CONFIGURATION-AS-DATA in the narrow sense
that survived the rebuild: FOUR columns carry a rule, and none of them is ever branched on by
NAME — that was the defect the first of them replaced.
RequiresExecutedDocument  read by the derived IsAwaitingDocument.
MustBeRoot / MustBeChild  where in the contract tree this type may sit. Mutually exclusive
(CK_ContractType_RootOrChild); BOTH FALSE means unrestricted, which
is the honest default and what two of these four want.
TemplateRequired         whether a contract of this type must carry its own ContractTemplateID.
MustBeRoot/MustBeChild REPLACED the three-state ParentStatusRequirement string (V202608200300,
ruled by Marcelo 2026-08-20): a column whose values invert the rule when read in the wrong order
is a column that will eventually be read in the wrong order.
ORDER FORM AND PAYMENT LINK ARE ACTIVE. They were retired (Status = Inactive) under R-4 on the
reasoning that contracts does no billing, so neither belonged. REVERSED by Marcelo 2026-08-20: both
are real agreement shapes regardless of who bills, and 7 of the 9 existing contracts use them.
Their two rule columns differ in exactly the way the columns exist to express:
Order Form    TemplateRequired = 1, RequiresExecutedDocument = 1  — incorporates the MA, and
somebody signs. Shows on Awaiting-documents until the file is registered.
Payment Link  TemplateRequired = 1, RequiresExecutedDocument = 0  — incorporates the MA, and
nobody signs. Never shows on Awaiting-documents. This is the ONLY type with
RequiresExecutedDocument = 0 and the reason that column exists.
Both previously carried TemplateRequired = 0, which contradicted their own descriptions: each one
says the agreement's terms live in the Master Agreement it references, and a contract whose terms
are entirely in a template it need not cite has no stated terms at all. Corrected here.
NOTE — R-5's live test is now gone. Retiring these two was deliberately doubling as the real-world
test of the Inactive-selection rule (a retired type still referenced by existing contracts). With
both Active, nothing exercises that path against real data; R-5's coverage is unit-level only until
some other type is retired or a fixture supplies one.
v1 seeded six types with fourteen columns of billing defaults (term months, billing frequency,
escalation percents, renewal mode, coterm). All of it is gone: v2 does not bill, does not renew
on a schedule, and does not decide anything from a type beyond whether paper is expected.
Fixed UUIDs so a re-push against a rebuilt database UPDATES these rows rather than creating a
second set. Deliberately a NEW block (3333…10xx) rather than reusing v1's 3333…000x.

fields.Name: Order Form
fields.Description: The commercial document a customer signs to buy — the ordinary agreement. Sits beneath a Master Agreement whose provisions it incorporates by reference, which is why the Order Form carries the ContractTemplateID rather than the MA carrying anything about it — hence TemplateRequired = 1. Signed paper is expected (RequiresExecutedDocument = 1), so it appears on the Awaiting-documents worklist until the executed file is registered. Reinstated Active 2026-08-20 (Marcelo), reversing the R-4 retirement.

fields.Name: Statement of Work
fields.Description: Scoped services with a defined end. Amith, 2026-08-18: SOWs have standard language but no versioned template — so an SOW contract may have no ContractTemplateID, and that is not a gap to fill. Paper is still expected.

fields.Name: Payment Link
fields.Description: The sub-$10k self-serve case: finance sends a HubSpot payment link that references the Master Agreement, and nobody signs anything. There is an implied contract, so it IS a contract — it carries a ContractTemplateID (TemplateRequired = 1, because the MA it incorporates is the only thing stating the terms) and no document. This is the one type where RequiresExecutedDocument is false, and the reason that column exists at all: it is what keeps a Payment Link OFF the Awaiting-documents worklist instead of sitting there forever waiting on paper that will never arrive. Reinstated Active 2026-08-20 (Marcelo), reversing the R-4 retirement; final shape pending Andrew's confirmation.

fields.Name: Change Order
fields.Description: Amends an existing agreement rather than replacing it: signed paper of its own, its own dates, and a ParentContractID naming what it changes. MustBeChild = 1 is what enforces that parent — the server subclass reads that flag, where it once compared this row's NAME to the string 'Change Order' and silently stopped working if anyone renamed it. It carries no template of its own (TemplateRequired = 0); a modification recorded on a change order may cite any provision of a template at or above it in the tree.
